source_locator.edition_or_translation: J. M. Ashmand translation from Proclus's Greek paraphrase; 1900 W. Foulsham & Co. new edition
source_locator.section: Faces, Chariots, and Other Similar Attributes of the Planets
source_locator.short_quote: each planet (although it may possess no familiarity with the sign encompassing it) is said to rejoice, when any connection subsists between itself and other stars of the same condition

prerequisites: connection between the planet and another star
calculation_dependencies: classification of the involved stars by planetary condition

condition.connection_target: another star of the same condition

normalized_rule: Classify a planet as rejoicing when a connection subsists between it and another star of the same condition.
synthesis_notes: This is a source-specific traditional classification, not scientific resonance evidence or a later house-planet joy scheme.
review_notes: Do not use WEST-PLANETARY-JOYS for this passage. The normalized rule is limited to the trigger on page 37; the explanatory continuation on page 38 is not needed to state the rule.
transmission_notes: The source's word 'rejoice' describes a Ptolemaic same-condition connection and is not automatically the later house-planet joy doctrine. The surrounding explanation continues onto page 38; certainty is scoped to the cited Ashmand/Proclus transmission.
